subject.title: [Bug]: Potential resource leak in runBoundTurnWithMissingThreadRecovery -- retry not wrapped in try/finally after thread spawn

question: Should Codex app-server conversation bindings keep a persistent subscription across turns, or should OpenClaw reattach before each bound turn and unsubscribe after each turn or failure?
rationale: The source issue is clear, but the repair changes subscription ownership for persistent bound conversations, and prior cleanup attempts showed that unconditional unsubscribe can break follow-up delivery.

options.title: Reattach Before Each Turn
options.body: Make each bound turn explicitly attach or resume the Codex app-server listener before turn/start, then allow cleanup on success and failure with two-turn regression coverage.

options.title: Keep Persistent Subscription
options.body: Treat the retained subscription as intentional lifecycle state, document or test that contract, and only clean up when the binding itself is cleared or abandoned.

options.title: Clear Binding On Retry Failure
options.body: On replacement retry rejection, unsubscribe and clear or mark the saved binding so the next inbound message creates a fresh thread instead of using an unsubscribed one.

recommendation.title: Reattach Before Each Turn
recommendation.body: Make each bound turn explicitly attach or resume the Codex app-server listener before turn/start, then allow cleanup on success and failure with two-turn regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to the original recovery commit as committer and to adjacent Codex app-server lifecycle work, making them the best available owner for the lifecycle direction call.
